title: JANUS Engine — TOPA + Spider magnetic-field / copper-vs-brass Axle pass
mission: Determine how a copper or brass Axle body changes the magnetic field and parasitic losses of the selected coreless AFPM / optional micro-EPM architecture.
Define a synchronized magnetic-field measurement protocol for the rotating Axle.
Separate static permanent-magnet field, stator-drive field, EPM switching transients and eddy-current reaction field.
Choose the preliminary structural conductor candidate without pretending to have measured JANUS hardware.

literature_anchors.finding: Copper C110-type samples measured about 57.2-57.6 MS/m while brass C260 measured about 15.5 MS/m at room temperature.
Coreless AFPM machines remove iron-core losses/cogging but require attention to electromagnetic leakage, winding loss and field topology.
Conductors exposed to the alternating air-gap field in slotless axial-flux machines develop additional eddy-current loss.
literature_anchors.role: direct warning for conductive structures near rotating/time-varying field

literature_anchors.finding: Coreless PCB axial-flux windings can incur substantial AC/eddy losses when copper is directly exposed to the rotating air-gap field.

physical_interpretation.copper_and_brass_magnetism: Copper and ordinary brass are approximately non-ferromagnetic, so they do not concentrate static flux like iron or electrical steel. Their main electromagnetic effect here is conductivity, not high permeability.
physical_interpretation.co_rotating_field_nuance: Permanent magnets rigidly mounted to the same Axle produce a field that is approximately stationary in the Axle material frame. In an ideal symmetric rotor this own-field component alone does not continuously sweep through the rotor body and therefore is not the main source of rotor eddy currents.
what_drives_eddy_currents: stator current field changing relative to the rotating Axle
spatial harmonics and asymmetry of the PM field
stationary conductive chamber or nearby metallic structures seeing the rotating PM field
transient acceleration/regeneration states and inverter harmonics
physical_interpretation.lenz_boundary: Any induced current creates a reaction field opposing the responsible field change and appears as drag/heat or altered field distribution; it is never free acceleration.

material_screen.interpretation: For otherwise comparable low-frequency geometry, copper has a much stronger tendency to support eddy currents than C260 brass. Exact drag/loss is geometry- and frequency-dependent and must not be inferred as a universal 3.71x loss ratio.
why: still non-ferromagnetic for the intended field geometry
better structural/machining role than soft high-conductivity copper in many rotor-body applications
material_screen.caution: Brass alloy selection must include dezincification/corrosion resistance in the actual low-hardness/DI-water chemistry. Do not freeze C260 specifically as the final wet-material alloy without corrosion testing.
material_screen.copper_role: retain copper where high electrical/thermal conductivity is deliberately useful, but electrically segment or isolate large closed current loops near the changing magnetic field where practical

skin_depth_screen.formula: delta = sqrt(1/(pi*f*mu0*sigma)) for a nonmagnetic conductor
skin_depth_screen.assumed_materials: sigma_Cu=57.5 MS/m, sigma_brass=15.5 MS/m, mu_r approximately 1
skin_depth_screen.interpretation: At the current JANUS 60-600 RPM screening range and 4-8 pole-pair examples, skin depth remains millimetres to centimetres rather than microscopic. A few-mm Axle shell therefore will not behave like a perfect magnetic shield, but closed conductive paths can still carry meaningful eddy currents and require measurement.

sensors: stationary calibrated 3-axis Hall / gauss probes for DC through low-frequency Bx, By, Bz
small search coil or equivalent dB/dt pickup for switching harmonics/transients
encoder index for rotor angle synchronization
Axle torque / drive power and rotor/chamber temperature
measurement_map.recommended_sample_rate: At least several kS/s for the first 60-600 RPM / <=80 Hz fundamental screen so harmonics and EPM pulses are not aliased; EPM pulse capture may require a separate faster transient channel.
probe_locations: near Axle magnetic ring / intended AFPM air gap
outside chamber housing as stray-field measurement
states: M0_BACKGROUND: Axle unmagnetized/de-energized where possible; measure ambient and sensor offset
M1_STATIC_PM: rotor stationary, coils off; map B(theta,r,z)
M2_PASSIVE_SPIN: external spin, drive coils off; isolate rotating-PM plus eddy reaction field
M3_MOTOR: battery/AFPM drives Axle at 60/120/300/600 RPM; measure field plus electrical input
M4_GENERATOR: independently driven Axle with regenerative load; map reaction field and recovered power
M5_EPM: optional micro-EPM assist; capture pulse dB/dt, residual field and heating
record_per_state: B_peak and B_RMS for each axis
vector magnitude and phase versus encoder angle

copper_vs_brass_A_B.principle: Use geometrically identical interchangeable conductive sleeves or representative coupons so material is the only intentional variable.
compare: incremental drive watts required for the same RPM
B waveform attenuation/phase shift at fixed probe points
copper_vs_brass_A_B.selection_metric: choose the wet structural material that minimizes electromagnetic parasitics plus corrosion/mechanical risk, not the material with the highest electrical conductivity

spider_verdict.field_measurement: MANDATORY; actual JANUS magnetic field in tesla cannot be honestly stated before magnet grade, geometry, air gap, pole count, coil current and hardware measurements/FEA are frozen.
spider_verdict.material_preference_now: brass-class lower-conductivity non-ferromagnetic structural body is a better first electromagnetic candidate than solid copper, subject to dezincification-resistant alloy selection and water compatibility
